lithia.title: As Crônicas de Líthia
lithia.short_intro: Moon’s long-running fantasy universe, with a canon of its own and a growing collection of stories.

ficcoes.title: Speculative Fiction
ficcoes.short_intro: Four distinct universes explore possible futures, contact, consciousness and alternative ways of organizing life together.

politica.title: Politics and Ideology
politica.short_intro: Ecos do Abismo examines Brazilian politics and the persistence of institutional mechanisms throughout recent history.

pensamento-lunar.title: Lunar Thought
pensamento-lunar.short_intro: Philosophy, sociology, psychology, history and religion make up Moon’s approach to the humanities, each with its own questions and sources.

ufologia.title: Ufology and Anomalous Phenomena
ufologia.short_intro: The Varginha case sits at the intersection of testimony, records, conflicting accounts and gaps in the evidence. The lines of inquiry remain hypotheses.

artigos.title: Academic Articles
artigos.short_intro: Research in academic formats on political history, psychology, affective modulation and human–AI cognition.

autobibliografia.title: Autobibliography
autobibliografia.short_intro: Projects in life writing that move through memory, identity, travel and relationships.

humano-ia.title: Human–AI Architecture
humano-ia.short_intro: Modernidades follows Moon from a childhood spent inventing things to building systems, with language at the heart of her experiments in human–AI collaboration.

laboratorios.title: Literary Laboratories
laboratorios.short_intro: Poetry, prose and fragments share this space with a partially preserved historical collection.

legado.title: Literary Legacy Before AI
legado.short_intro: Three early works in their original self-published editions. Any new editions follow a separate editorial path.

psicodelicos.title: Psychedelics
psicodelicos.short_intro: Psicanábis and Luz da Lótus are companion works whose writing conditions form part of the author’s method.

tabus.title: Taboos
tabus.short_intro: Anatomia do Proibido explores how social, moral, historical and cultural boundaries are formed and contested.
